title: segmented-block-pool: dynamic eviction with kernel-aware allocation and soft-pinning
author: Lena Park
description: Motivation: reduce KV cache churn and tail latency for mixed workloads by introducing a segmented block pool that separates hot/cold pages and applies kernel-aware allocation hints. This PR implements a soft-pinning layer plus a dynamic eviction policy that accounts for model kernel usage patterns and sequence-length locality. Design highlights: 1) segmented_pool component maintains two logical segments (hot/cold) and migrates blocks based on access frequency and active kernel hints; 2) eviction policy is LRU-ST (LRU with sequence-time decay) so short-lived prefixes don't evict long-running contexts; 3) kernel-aware allocation: callers can attach an allocation hint (e.g. attention-optimized, kv-dense) that biases allocator to choose blocks that match the downstream execution path (reduces rematerialization and kernel fallback); 4) soft-pinning: soft pins mark blocks as preferred for a short window and are honored unless memory pressure forces forced eviction; soft pins are used for canary in-flight requests to avoid thrashing; 5) quotas: per-model soft quotas and burst-reserve to avoid noisy-neighbor regressions. Rollout approach: staged rollout behind a feature flag default-off, smoke tests in Dedicated, canary in Hosted for <100 accounts first, metric gates for increased traffic. Backwards compatibility: falls back to existing paged allocator when flag disabled. Testing and benchmarks: microbench harness added plus cluster-level perf job. Observed improvements: p50 latency for multi-turn chat workload down 9-14% and sustained throughput up 6-9% for batching window=20. CPU overhead small (~1-2% on scheduler path) while reducing GPU stalls from poor KV reuse. See files changed for details and benchmarks.

motivation_context: This targets recurring incidents where mixed small/long sequences caused prefix eviction of long-running KV contexts leading to expensive recompute on GPU kernels. Prior approaches (single paged allocator, softpin v1) reduced some churn but still allowed corner-case oscillation; segmented approach with kernel hints aligns allocator decisions with downstream kernel execution patterns and preserves long-lived contexts.
